summary: ARES-MED (Autonomous Real-Time Evaluation & Space Medical Decision System) is an offline-first web platform that acts as a medical copilot for deep-space crews. On Mars missions, messages to Earth can take up to 44 minutes round trip, and standard medical tools misread microgravity physiology. Fluids shift toward the head, and cabin CO₂ can mimic common illnesses. ARES-MED fuses astronaut vitals with spacecraft air and radiation data and adapts baselines to gravity, mission day, and sex. It then generates instant three-stage prescriptions, exportable as a PDF and an HL7 FHIR packet. Users pick an astronaut avatar, explore five space crises on an interactive body map, and try three tools: a webcam and voice vitals scan, a NASA PVT-based reaction test, and a 30-day treatment simulation. Everything runs locally in the browser. Thresholds trace to NASA-STD-3001, the Twins Study, OSDR, and TRISH HERMES. It matters because it gives crews medical autonomy during communication blackouts, and it also serves rural clinics and anyone curious about space health, in English and Turkish.
details:
ARES-MED lets users choose an astronaut avatar and one of five space crises (CO₂ scrubber fault, solar storm, eye and bone shift, sleep debt, nominal transit). An interactive body map then shows how each organ responds under 0g, Moon, or Mars gravity, adjusted for mission day and sex. Users can run a webcam and voice vitals scan, take a NASA PVT-based reaction test, or simulate 30 days of treatment choices. A four-step self-diagnosis wizard produces an immediate, short-term, and follow-up care plan, exportable as a PDF and an HL7 FHIR file.

Benefits and impact: Crews get medical guidance during 44-minute communication blackouts, and the same offline triage can serve rural clinics. It also makes space medicine understandable for students and the public.

Tools: We used web technologies (WebRTC camera rPPG, WebAudio voice analysis, and HL7 FHIR export), with all processing running locally in the browser. Data came from NASA-STD-3001, the Twins Study, OSDR, and TRISH HERMES.

Creativity: Instead of complex telemetry consoles that only flight surgeons can interpret, ARES-MED translates deep-space medicine into an intuitive, visual interface accessible to everyone curious about space, fusing human vitals with spacecraft air and radiation sensors, interactive anatomical organ callouts, and a hands-on astronaut lab.

Factors considered: strict local privacy (zero data uploaded), 100% offline execution, 0g and sex-adapted physiological baselines, human-in-the-loop clinical escalation, and bilingual accessibility (English and Turkish).
